task.title: Review and fix a buggy Android 'My orders' screen
task.brief: This Kotlin ViewModel and Fragment show a customer's orders in a delivery app. Users report crashes on slow or no network, the list reloading on every rotation, and a memory leak. In about 25 minutes, list each problem you see, explain why it happens, and write the corrected code (it does not need to compile perfectly). A good answer covers threading and coroutine scope, lifecycle and rotation, error and loading states, memory leaks, and how the UI should observe data.
key_points: Holding MainActivity in the ViewModel leaks it; remove it and send UI events instead of Toasts
ViewModel built with a constructor call is not retained; use by viewModels() / ViewModelProvider
GlobalScope is not tied to the screen; use viewModelScope
Blocking execute() on Dispatchers.Main causes NetworkOnMainThreadException or ANR; use a suspend call on IO
body()!! crashes on errors or empty body; check isSuccessful and catch IOException
Expose loading, success and error state to the UI
observe(this) in a Fragment should use viewLifecycleOwner
Avoid reloading on every view creation; load once (init or when data is empty)

rubric.label: Bugs found and fixed
rubric.guide: 0 = no real bugs found, 3 = threading or crash fixed but lifecycle issues missed, 5 = threading, crash, leak and rotation all fixed

rubric.label: Lifecycle understanding
rubric.guide: 0 = ignores rotation and leaks, 3 = fixes ViewModel creation only, 5 = proper ViewModel, viewLifecycleOwner and load-once logic

rubric.label: Errors and edge cases
rubric.guide: 0 = no error handling, 3 = try/catch only, 5 = clear loading, error and empty states with safe parsing

rubric.label: Explanation
rubric.guide: 0 = code only or unclear, 3 = some reasons given, 5 = each fix clearly explained in plain words
